# Prompt - Cohere command-a API

This simple example demonstrates how to prompt [Cohere](https://cohere.com/)
using their client API. It performs a single prompt and does not engage in a
conversational exchange with the model.

The example directly utilises Cohere’s specific API, which may result in the
application being tightly coupled to this particular model unless an abstraction
layer is implemented. A more flexible approach would be to use an API such as
[langchain4j](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j) or
[Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai).

This example connects to a publicly hosted instance of Cohere’s AI. An API
key—available from
[Cohere’s dashboard](https://dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys)—is required. At the
time of writing, Cohere offers a generous free tier, which is more than
sufficient for this use case.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Cohere API Key](https://dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

## Run the example

1. Cohere API Key

   If you have not already done so, please create an API key from
   [Cohere’s dashboard](https://dashboard.cohere.com/api-keys). This example
   searches for the key in the following order:

    1. System property: `cohere.api.key`
       (e.g. `java -Dcohere.api.key=[API-KEY] ...`)
    2. Environment variable: `COHERE_API_KEY`
       (e.g. `COHERE_API_KEY=[API-KEY] java ...`)
    3. File: `~/.cohere/api.key`

   For security purposes and to prevent exposing the API key in documentation,
   the following commands assume the key is saved in the `.cohere/api.key` file
   within the user’s home directory.

   Verify that the Cohere APIs can be successfully invoked. The following
   command assumes that the API key is stored at `~/.cohere/api.key`.

   ```shell
   curl --request POST \
     --silent \
     --url https://api.cohere.ai/v2/chat \
     --header 'accept: application/json' \
     --header 'content-type: application/json' \
     --header "Authorization: bearer $(cat ~/.cohere/api.key)" \
     --data '{
     "model": "command-a-03-2025",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
       }
     ]
   }' | jq
   ```

   The model response

   ```json
   {
     "id": "98eca6e1-8f13-441e-9ec2-375d4764df27",
     "message": {
       "role": "assistant",
       "content": [
         {
           "type": "text",
           "text": "Humans first landed on the Moon on **July 20, 1969**, as part of the **Apollo 11** mission. Astronauts **Neil Armstrong** and **Buzz Aldrin** became the first humans to set foot on the lunar surface, while **Michael Collins** remained in orbit around the Moon in the command module. Armstrong famously declared, \"That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind,\" as he took his first steps on the Moon. This historic event marked the culmination of the United States' Apollo program and the Space Race with the Soviet Union."
         }
       ]
     },
     "finish_reason": "COMPLETE",
     "usage": {
       "billed_units": {
         "input_tokens": 9,
         "output_tokens": 123
       },
       "tokens": {
         "input_tokens": 504,
         "output_tokens": 125
       },
       "cached_tokens": 0
     }
   }
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that a valid Cohere API key is available at
   `~/.cohere/api.key`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do this.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file and its dependencies.

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── annotations-13.0.jar
   ├── cohere-java-1.10.1.jar
   ├── jackson-annotations-2.18.6.jar
   ├── jackson-core-2.18.6.jar
   ├── jackson-databind-2.18.6.jar
   ├── jackson-datatype-jdk8-2.18.6.jar
   ├── jackson-datatype-jsr310-2.18.6.jar
   ├── kotlin-stdlib-2.2.21.jar
   ├── okhttp-5.2.1.jar
   ├── okhttp-jvm-5.3.2.jar
   ├── okio-3.16.1.jar
   ├── okio-jvm-3.16.4.jar
   └── prompt-command-a-api-1.0.0.jar

   1 directory, 13 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that a valid Cohere API key is available at
   `~/.cohere/api.key`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do this.

   Run the example with the default prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   Although the prompt remains the same, the output may vary with each run.

   ```
   prompt> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   assistant> Humans first landed on the Moon on **July 20, 1969**, as part of the **Apollo 11** mission. Astronauts **Neil Armstrong** and **Buzz Aldrin** became the first humans to set foot on the lunar surface, while **Michael Collins** remained in orbit around the Moon in the command module. Armstrong's first words upon stepping onto the Moon, *"That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind,"* have become iconic in history. This achievement marked a major milestone in space exploration and the culmination of the United States' Apollo program.
   ```

   Run the example again with specific prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main 'Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?'
   ```

   The model should respond with 'Neil Armstrong', as he was the first person to
   walk on the Moon.

   ```
   prompt> Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
   assistant> The first person to walk on the Moon was **Neil Armstrong**, an American astronaut. On **July 20, 1969**, Armstrong, as commander of the **Apollo 11** mission, made history by stepping onto the lunar surface and uttering the famous words, *"That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind."* He was followed shortly after by his fellow astronaut, **Buzz Aldrin**, while the third member of the crew, **Michael Collins**, remained in orbit around the Moon in the command module.
   ```
